rows.what the ink shows: The parenthetical phrase begins with a long descending p and a short upright in its compressed ending. The next word has a tall looped b and a long low body ending in two rises. The following word shows a small initial loop, a separated upper mark, a p-like downstroke and a final rise, followed by a separate short de before K. These visible word divisions and distinctive stems support partie bornée dépendant de.

The opening of the deleted passage has a long descending initial stroke with an upper loop and several smaller strokes around the heavy horizontal deletion. The central letter bodies lie under that line, while an overlapping raised run contributes additional uprights. Even in the 4× detail these strokes do not separate securely into prolongeant, so the original uncertainty is retained.

Immediately before the separately written φ_i, a small ascending loop returns into a low connected tail. The loop remains above the cancellation and the short tail below it; its compact l-plus-es form is also present in the later les before φ_i on this page.

At the right end after et, the raised run has a short curved opening, an isolated upper dot and a sequence of low humps. Beneath it a thick cancellation crosses another set of tall stems and an extended lower curve. The two writing levels and the strike conceal the middle letter sequence; the visible fragments do not securely establish considérant.

Before the next φ_i, the first word retains a crossed initial upright, a connected low body and a second short upright near its middle. It is followed after a clear space by a curved ascending l returning into a short horizontal tail, matching the compact les earlier on this page. The t positions and separate l-tail support toutes les despite the cancellation crossing the start.

After φ_f the terminal glyph has two close tall strokes forming a narrow upper opening, a long descending stroke reaching the box baseline, and several dense rightward strokes at mid-height. At 6× enlargement the central overtracing is inseparable; a clean ξ contour cannot be isolated, and no different literal reading is secure.

The first word retains two raised strokes with small rounded fragments between them, but its baseline is covered by a broad horizontal strike and the later diagonal cancellation. The final word has a low beginning followed by two distinct l ascenders and a short connected terminal tail, sufficient for nulles. The first word remains uncertain rather than being inferred from the phrase.

Several thick, nearly coincident horizontal cancellation strokes cover the bodies and joins of this phrase. A few upright tips and a dot survive above them, and one hooked descender survives below near the middle, compatible with the g of voisinage; the surrounding letters and the short outer words cannot be separated securely even at 4×.

At the end of the rotated proposition, after il suffit, the writing reduces to overlapping hooked/looped strokes and a short rightward mark; tall strokes from the intersecting main writing also enter the margin. The enlarged line does not provide distinct letter groups sufficient to verify all three proposed words or to replace them with a different phrase.

The deleted capital has an upright stem and a strong diagonal lower-right leg. Two crossing cancellation strokes obscure the upper-right region where an R bowl would have to close, so the exposed strokes could also belong to K. A paired lobed mark is visible raised to its right, supporting the infinity superscript but not resolving the capital.

Above a struck-through remnant after prop. 3, the surviving reading begins with a small open cup rising into a narrow loop, followed by a tall rounded d-like stroke. The following low linked strokes and separate shallow terminal curl support the ci-dessus sequence; it is the writing above the cancellation that is read here.

Immediately before the two parallel bars, the word has only a shallow initial bowl/crest followed by a long almost level exit. There is no securely separate second hump or internal loop that distinguishes n from a rapidly contracted m, and the terminal e is flattened into the exit. The source ne remains uncertain.

The first group begins with an upright t-like stroke, has a long low join that bends below the baseline into the j region, and ends in a small rightward s-like hook. A separate tall curved l and its low return follow, then a tall f with a descending hook and extended low continuation. These three separated groups support toujours la forme.

At the next line start, a long descending initial p returns sharply upward; two small dots sit over the compressed interior strokes. The latter portion has a narrow loop/rounded join, then a tall final l with a low rightward curl, supporting principale.

notes.notes: All seven assigned marks were personally inspected in enlarged bands; additional details target ambiguous cancellation and glyph strokes. M0278 was sent to the coordinator for independent inspection before completing the remaining work. M0274 and M0276 retain uncertainty because the cancellation and overlapping writing obscure their sequences; M0279 is narrowed to uncertainty on toutes. No unmarked corrections are proposed. No OCR, Hua comparison, page commit or next-page inspection was performed.

notes: Read only assigned M0280–M0286 on scan016; no OCR or text recognition used. Source image dimensions 1758×1891.

Rotation -90 degrees means clockwise in Pillow; every box is in the actual unrotated source coordinates. Inspection timestamps are the actual clock readings obtained immediately after the corresponding batch was displayed.
Independent checks requested for M0281, M0282 and M0284. Initial submitted readings preserve uncertainty; coordinator may reconcile after its own inspection.
The writing represented by M0283 is above a canceled remnant at the same marked location. No unmarked correction was made or asserted.

reconciliations: All four independent checks remain undecided. No new surviving discriminator warrants another inspection.

M0278 and M0281 agree exactly. M0282 peer explicitly lists R/K with a visible infinity superscript; primary whole proposed R^infinity remains uncertain and its observations already identify the same capital ambiguity. M0284 peer lists ne/me while primary keeps ne uncertain and records the n/m ambiguity. Both reports are retained without asserting certainty or consensus on hidden letters.
Every primary row contains adequate own-ink observations; no unchanged uncertainty is interpreted as a positive confirmation of its candidate. No unmarked page content is changed.
